## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r}
### import libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(readr)
# Primary schools (from mainstream xlsx)
primary <- read_excel("./DATA/Data_on_Individual_Schools_Mainstream_2024_25.xlsx",
                      sheet = "Mainstream Schools", skip = 0) %>%   # ← change to 0
  rename(roll_number = `Roll Number`,
         name        = `Official Name`,
         places      = `Enrolment per Return`,
         lat         = `School Latitude`,
         lon         = `School Longitude`) %>%
  mutate(places = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(places))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon), !is.na(places), places > 0) %>%
  select(roll_number, name, places, lat, lon)
# Post-primary schools (from eircode CSV)
post_primary <- read.csv("./DATA/School_Data_Eircode_2024_2025.csv", 
                         fileEncoding = "latin1") %>%
  mutate(places = as.numeric(gsub(",", "", Total.2024.2025))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(School.Latitude), !is.na(School.Longitude), !is.na(places), places > 0) %>%
  select(roll_number = Roll.Number,
         name        = Official.School.Name,
         places,
         lat         = School.Latitude,
         lon         = School.Longitude)
# Combine into single sf object
schools_sf <- bind_rows(primary, post_primary) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
# CSA centroids for r5r origins
sa <- st_read("./DATA/Small_Area_National_Statistical_Boundaries_2022.geojson", quiet = TRUE)
csa_centroids <- st_centroid(sa)
# Quick check
cat("Total schools:", nrow(schools_sf), "\n")
cat("CSA centroids:", nrow(csa_centroids), "\n")
```
##schools_Sf
#Loaded primary schools from the xlsx (3,081 schools)
#Loaded post-primary from the eircode CSV (723 schools)
#Combined into one schools_sf object → 3,804 schools total

##csa_centriods
#Read the CSA boundary GeoJSON
#Extracted the centroid (centre point) of each polygon → 18,919 centroids

#all schools as spatial points with enrolment - school_sf
#one point per CSA, ready to use as origins in r5r - csa_centroids

You can also embed plots, for example:
```{r save-outputs}
saveRDS(schools_sf,    "./DATA/schools_sf.rds")
saveRDS(csa_centroids, "./DATA/csa_centroids.rds")
cat("Saved successfully\n")
```
```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# Load saved data from data_prep
schools_sf      <- readRDS("./DATA/schools_sf.rds")
csa_centroids   <- readRDS("./DATA/csa_centroids.rds")

# r5r needs data frames with specific columns: id, lon, lat
origins <- csa_centroids %>%
  st_transform(4326) %>%
  mutate(
    id  = as.character(SA_PUB2022),
    lon = st_coordinates(.)[,1],
    lat = st_coordinates(.)[,2]
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(id, lon, lat)

destinations <- schools_sf %>%
  st_transform(4326) %>%
  mutate(
    id  = as.character(roll_number),
    lon = st_coordinates(.)[,1],
    lat = st_coordinates(.)[,2]
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(id, lon, lat, places)

cat("Origins:", nrow(origins), "\n")
cat("Destinations:", nrow(destinations), "\n")
```
SA_PUB2022 — CSA identifier (used to join everything)
roll_number, name, places, lat, lon — school columns
schools_sf and csa_centroids as the two spatial objects
